notes: Phase 0 of docs/model-eval-baseline-proposal.md: baseline run-to-run variance only.
One arm, one brief, one base, three repetitions. No arm is compared to anything here.
Purpose: until the baseline spread on an identical brief is known, no Phase A difference
can be called a difference rather than noise. Read the spread in deterministic delivery,
repair count, retry count and wall time across the three identical runs.
If the baseline is bimodal on an identical brief, Phase A needs more repetitions or
narrower cases - and learning that costs 6 runs here instead of 24 there.
Every repositoryPath is a dedicated eval worktree pinned at that case's frozen base,
not the operator's live checkout. Task creation requires HEAD == frozenBaseSha, so the
checkout has to sit still for the whole of a case's arms; doing that in a live checkout
would detach the branch an operator or another agent is working on. A disposable
worktree can be moved between cases freely and is not shared with any other work.

cases.title: Prompt A — shared-remedy fee grouping
cases.description:
Implement shared-remedy fee grouping in eversor-plancheck. Branch off
evesor-plancheck/main (the remote is `evesor-plancheck`, NOT origin).

Problem: when six claims are all closed by one deliverable — one Schedule of
Prices, one responsibility matrix — each claim currently carries its own
PRODUCE_SCHEDULE fee and the tender's remedy subtotal bills it six times. Every
claim must be retained; only the fee is counted once.

FOLLOW THE EXISTING PATTERN, do not invent one. Construction pricing already
solved the equivalent problem: read backend/variation_costs/aggregation.py,
which groups by `change_group_id` (a reviewer-set group) falling back to
`event_key`, counts one amount per event, reports `shared_claims`, and marks a
group `disputed` when members disagree rather than silently picking one.
Mirror that design and its safety property.

Requirements:
- A reviewer attaches claims to a named remedy group with one common
  deliverable and one editable fee. Append-only revisions, consistent with
  backend/remedy_prices' existing revision model.
- The fee counts ONCE per group in every subtotal. Separately-priced extra work
  on a member claim is preserved and still counted.
- No claim is deleted, hidden or merged. A grouped claim still renders.
- Where members disagree, follow aggregation.py: report it, do not pick one.
- Surface the group and the shared count on Review, All Tenders and Command
  Deck, and make the three agree. Read backend/deck/ and backend/tenders/
  measurements.py (`cost_to_close`) — they must not double-count.
- dbmate migration for any new table. Never create tables from Python.

Read AGENTS.md and backend/AGENTS.md first. backend/remedy_prices/models.py's
docstring states the invariants — the table prices the FIX, never what the
variation is worth unfixed. Do not add a confidence, probability or expected
value field.

Verify: python -m pytest, make integration-test (asserts zero skips),
cd frontend && npm run test, make backend-quality, npm run api:types.
`make e2e-native` has a floor of 2 failed (03-tender-parity colspan, broken on
main too) — that is not your regression.

Report before/after remedy subtotals per tender. Do not merge. No detection,
REMEDY, adjudication or model runs. No Azure changes.
acceptanceCriteria: A shared remedy group counts its deliverable fee exactly once in every subtotal.
No claim is deleted, hidden or merged; a grouped claim still renders.
Disagreeing group members are reported as disputed rather than silently resolved.
Review, All Tenders and Command Deck agree on the group and its shared count.
Any new table arrives via a dbmate migration, never from Python.
